Import Bank Statement / POS File

Upload, extract, review, categorize, verify, then approve. Nothing posts directly to the ledger.

BCF verification rule: imported files only create a temporary review queue. Every selected transaction must pass the review screen and a final posting verification before the official ledger changes.

1. Choose an import file

Use CSV when your bank/POS provides it. For now, BCF can also extract text from text-based PDF bank statements. Scanned/image-only PDFs will need OCR in a later build.

2. Confirm CSV column mapping

Verify Extracted Transactions

Receipt Split Helper

Use this when one receipt contains purchases for more than one expense category. Each split will be previewed first, then each approved line posts as its own ledger line while sharing the same receipt reference.

Example: Costco receipt → Snack Bar Food + Drinks + Supplies.

Shows bank balance movement plus the accounting P&L for the selected period.

Backup & Export

Move the same BCF books between your iPhone and laptop.

BCF_Index.html is the program. Your BCF backup JSON file is your books.
On iPhone, BACKUP BOOKS opens the Share sheet when supported so you can save the backup directly to Google Drive or Files. On your laptop, restore that same JSON file to load the identical books.

Opening Bank Balance

This is the bank balance immediately before BCF's first ledger transaction. It is a balance-forward value, not income, so it never appears on the P&L.

BACKUP BOOKS

Creates the complete portable BCF backup: ledger, sponsors, categories, events, duplicate protection, and settings.

Export Ledger CSV

A spreadsheet copy that opens in Excel, Google Sheets, and Apple Numbers.

Restore BCF Books

Select a BCF JSON backup from Files, Google Drive, iCloud Drive, or your computer.

Local Data

BCF automatically saves changes inside the browser/device you are currently using. A backup is what transfers those books to another device.
